q-47954.name: Question 1
q-47954.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\sqrt{x})^{′}\cdot {e}^{x}+\sqrt{x}\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}{e}^{x}+\sqrt{x}{e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}+2x{e}^{x}}{2\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

x+2exx
e

Submit
Correct

f′(x)=(x)′⋅ex+x⋅(ex)′=12xex+xex=ex+2xex2x

q-48516.name: Question 2
q-48516.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
q-48516.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi } & ={{e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)|}_{x=\pi } \\  & ={e}^{\pi }(-1+0) \\  & =-{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-{e}^{\pi }.$

q-48516.html:
Question 2
?

If a curve C is given by y=exsin⁡x, calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where x=π.

a
eπ
b
πeπ
c
−eπ
d
0
e
−πeπ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We differentiate using the product rule. Let u(x)=ex and v(x)=sin⁡x. Then, we have

dudx=ex,dvdx=cos⁡x.

Applying the product rule gives

dydx=udvdx+vdudx=ex⋅cos⁡x+(sin⁡x)⋅ex=ex(cos⁡x+sin⁡x).

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute x=π into the formula and get

dydx|x=π=ex(cos⁡x+sin⁡x)|x=π=eπ(−1+0)=−eπ.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is −eπ.

q-311231.name: Question 3
q-311231.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={3}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({3}^{x})}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+{3}^{x}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))}^{′} \\  & =({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3))\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+{3}^{x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)) \\  & ={3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-{3}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

3xln(3)cos(x)
−3xsin⁡(x)

Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=3x and v(x)=cos⁡(x). So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(3x)′cos⁡(x)+3x(cos⁡(x))′=(3xln⁡(3))cos⁡(x)+3x(−sin⁡(x))=3xln⁡(3)cos⁡(x)−3xsin⁡(x)
